land.text: Hungary within the post-Trianon frontiers, to which the 1947 Paris treaty restored it ('reduced to its immediate post-Trianon borders'), less three villages near Bratislava

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's 'Hungarian Republic' row (1919-1943, Wikipedia title Hungary) is the Kingdom of Hungary of the regency; 'The Second Hungarian Republic ... Predecessor: Kingdom of Hungary'. Its shapes stop in 1943: Hungary has no Cliopatria shape for 1944-1945.

land.text: the whole country within the frontiers of the 1947 Paris peace treaty, renamed the Hungarian People's Republic when the constitution was promulgated on 20 August 1949

successors.note: The Second Republic page's infobox also lists Democratic Federal Yugoslavia and the Third Czechoslovak Republic as successors, but names no territory for them; the only land the pages move is the three villages near Bratislava (ledger 1947).

capitals.name: Budapest
capitals.note: 'Capital and largest city: Budapest' (infobox); the coordinates are the city's, not the infobox's.

correction.text: Hungary within the post-Trianon frontiers, 93,073 km2 in 1946 by the infobox; the 1947 outline is used because the three villages near Bratislava were ceded only with the 1947 treaty

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, shape taken from 1947: Cliopatria's Hungary row begins in 1947 but the page dates the republic from 1 February 1946 and gives '1946: 93,073 km2' against '1947 and 1949: 93,011 km2'. The 62 km2 between the two figures is the 62 km2 of the three villages (Bratislava bridgehead page). The three villages are far below the 252 km2 cell size, so the 1947 outline stands for 1946.

91,985 km2 for 1947-1949 against the infobox's 93,011 km2 for 1947 and 1949 (ratio 0.99). The frontier is the Trianon one that the Paris treaty (10 February 1947) restored ('Hungary's borders were moved back to those that existed on 1 January 1938'); the three villages near Bratislava go to Czechoslovakia (ledger). Cliopatria's Hungary row resumes in 1990 (dossier hungary, the Third Republic); 1950-1989 is the Hungarian People's Republic row (dossier hungarian-people-s-republic), whose 1949 keyframe overlaps this one from 20 August 1949.

ledger.note: 1946: the Second Hungarian Republic replaces the Kingdom. It was 'briefly established after the disestablishment of the Kingdom of Hungary on 1 February 1946'; 'the Republic was proclaimed in the aftermath of the Soviet occupation of Hungary' (Red Army occupation 'from September 1944 until April 1945'). The page gives the date, not a frontier; the country is drawn at its infobox area of 93,073 km2.

region.text: the three villages south-east of Bratislava, Dunacsún (Čunovo), Horvátjárfalu (Jarovce) and Oroszvár (Rusovce), 62 km2

ledger.note: 1947: Hungary cedes three villages near Bratislava to Czechoslovakia under the Paris treaty ('three villages near Bratislava were also transferred to Czechoslovakia'; treaties signed 10 February 1947, effective 15 September 1947). The Bratislava bridgehead page names Čunovo, Jarovce and Rusovce and gives 62 km2, 'only the first three were granted to them', and the Second Hungarian Republic infobox falls from 93,073 km2 (1946) to 93,011 km2 (1947). The month is the treaty's effective date, a reading; the area is below the grid's cell size.

region.text: the whole country, whose land passes unchanged to the Hungarian People's Republic

ledger.note: 1949: the Second Republic ends and the Hungarian People's Republic follows. 'It was itself dissolved on 20 August 1949 and succeeded by the Soviet-backed Hungarian People's Republic' (infobox 'People's Republic: 20 August 1949'); the People's Republic page: 'When it was officially promulgated on 20 August, the country was renamed the "Hungarian People's Republic."' and names the Second Hungarian Republic as predecessor. The People's Republic is a separate dossier (hungarian-people-s-republic): a new state on the same land, not a rename.

certainty.note: Pre-1938 (Trianon) frontier restored in fact under Soviet occupation; the formal restoration followed with the treaty of 1947.
The frontier is the Trianon one as confirmed on 10 February 1947 (effective 15 September 1947) with the three villages near Bratislava ceded.

sources.title: Second Hungarian Republic
sources.note: Established 1 February 1946, dissolved 20 August 1949; area 93,073 km2 (1946), 93,011 km2 (1947, 1949); Soviet occupation Sep 1944-Apr 1945; Paris treaty 10 February 1947.

sources.title: Paris Peace Treaties, 1947
sources.note: Signed 10 February 1947, effective 15 September 1947; Hungary restored to its pre-1938 borders, Vienna Awards void, three villages near Bratislava to Czechoslovakia.

sources.title: Hungarian People's Republic
sources.note: Renamed 20 August 1949; Republic of Hungary established 23 October 1989; no border changes.

sources.title: Bratislava bridgehead
sources.note: Czechoslovakia obtained Čunovo, Jarovce and Rusovce, 62 km2; the page gives no date.

notes: Second Hungarian Republic, 1 February 1946 to 20 August 1949, split off on 2026-11-01 from the dossier 'hungary' after the reviewer failed it: that dossier called 1949 and 1989 renames while hungarian-people-s-republic held the same land for forty years (two states on one land). The Cliopatria row 'Hungary' (Q28513, shapes 1947-1949 and 1990-2024) is therefore split by years: this dossier reviews hungary_1947 (1947-1949) and a new 1946 keyframe; the dossier hungary is the Third Republic from 23 October 1989 and reviews hungary_1990 onward. Wikidata is null here (the id of the row stays with hungary; wikidata.org is unreachable). For the other eu-22 part: hungarian-people-s-republic should change its predecessor from hungary to second-hungarian-republic (its page names 'Second Hungarian Republic' as predecessor) and the counterpart of its 1949 found event; its successor hungary is already right. Not settled: Hungary has no Cliopatria shape for 1944-1945 (the Red Army occupied Hungary 'from September 1944 until April 1945', Second Republic page), so the Hungarian state of 1944-1945 (and the 1946 keyframe's predecessor shape) belongs to whoever owns hungarian-republic; the exact transfer date of the three villages (the Bratislava bridgehead page gives 62 km2 and no date; the Paris treaty took effect 15 September 1947, the ledger's month is that effective date, a reading); the matching gain in the czechoslovakia dossier (its ledger has no 1947 event from Hungary; for eu-21); the successors the infobox lists besides the People's Republic (Democratic Federal Yugoslavia, Third Czechoslovak Republic) are not applied because the page names no land for them; heads of state are not on the pages opened, so no ruler strip. Page-dated quotes re-opened in the repair pass: Second Hungarian Republic (1 February 1946; 20 August 1949; 93,073 / 93,011 km2), Hungarian People's Republic ('People's Republic: 20 August 1949'; predecessor Second Hungarian Republic), Paris Peace Treaties ('three villages (namely Horvatjarfalu, Oroszvar, and Dunacsun) situated south of Bratislava'; effective 15 September 1947), Bratislava bridgehead ('Only the first three were granted to them, and they acquired a territory of 62 km2 of Hungary'). Gazetteer names: none missing.
